summary.headline: Birlasoft Q4 FY26 revenue flat QoQ at INR 13,486 mn with EBITDA margin up to 18.5%, while FY26 revenue fell 1.2% in INR and TCV reached $208 mn.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was $145.3 mn, down 3.7% QoQ in constant currency, though INR revenue rose 0.1% QoQ to INR 1,348.6 crore on currency tailwinds. EBITDA margin expanded 30 bps QoQ to 18.5%, helped by forex (about 170 bps) and one-off provision reversals (about 170 bps) per management. FY26 revenue declined 6% in dollars and 1.2% in rupees, with about 200 bps of growth removed by exiting low-margin, non-strategic deals. Management said demand remains very soft and it does not give revenue guidance; the focus shifts to sales expansion (sellers up 30-40%) and order booking.

segments.name: Energy & Utilities (E&U)
segments.commentary: Only vertical to grow sequentially in Q4, up 1.8% QoQ; management cited it as doing well.

segments.name: Life Sciences (MedTech / medical devices)
segments.commentary: Source of the client-specific operational issue and the biggest degrowth; management believes the bad news is behind it, but it is a manufacturing-oriented sub-sector.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Degrew in Q4 on macro headwinds; management says a large portion of new sellers will be added in US manufacturing.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Degrew in Q4 on furloughs in Q3 and fewer working days; mainly T&M. Focus areas are payments, asset management and P&C insurance; management expects it to become a strong growth vertical.

segments.name: ERP
segments.commentary: Described as consistently underperforming; a new 25-year SAP veteran leader was hired, with the aim of returning it to growth.

guidance_outlook: No revenue guidance given; management cites volatility and says it does not guide for smaller companies.

Steady-state EBITDA margin expected to be 15% plus, with erosion from current 18.5% due to sales, leadership and AI-orchestration investments, ramp-up effects and front-ended productivity commitments.
Sales team expected to grow 30-40% YoY by mid-FY27; about 40% more sellers by end of Q2 FY27.
H2 expected to be stronger for order booking as in prior years; management hopes FY27 will be better but did not commit to a quarterly revenue path.
Lower ETR from FY27 as incremental US federal tax provision is limited to FY26.
Q4 one-off benefits (about 340 bps total, incl. ~170 bps forex) will not recur; forex is not being predicted for Q1.
risks_watch: Revenue continues to decline; management has not committed to any quarterly growth timeline, and this is the sixth quarter without QoQ growth.
Margin sustainability: Q4 benefited from about 340 bps of one-offs and forex; the CFO guides to 15% plus as steady state.
Whether the 30-40% sales headcount ramp converts into pipeline and order booking in H1 FY27.
Client concentration and the Life Sciences / MedTech client issue; management says it will not recur but cannot disclose details.
Capital allocation: the Board has not signalled a decision on surplus cash; the final dividend is subject to shareholder approval.
AI deal pricing: up-front productivity commitments and outcome-based fixed-price deals may keep compressing revenue.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the top line: management openly says it is disappointed and that FY26 fell short on revenue. It is confident on margins and the new sales and leadership hires, but refuses to give revenue or order-book guidance, citing volatility.

It's not that we have lost any deals. It's just getting pushed to Q1.
we are at the bottom of the pit right now, as you said.

qa_highlights.question: Girish Pai (BOB Capital) asked whether FY27 revenue growth will be positive and how it will phase across quarters or halves.
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no revenue guidance. It cited the exit from unprofitable deals, AI upfront productivity giveaways and account-specific issues; H2 is usually stronger for order booking, while H1 revenue is hard to call. Management hopes the bad news is behind it and FY27 will be better.

qa_highlights.question: Sudheer Guntupalli (Kotak) asked which vertical had the client-specific issue and whether it is fully behind.
qa_highlights.answer: The issue was in Life Sciences, specifically MedTech/medical devices, which is manufacturing-oriented. Management believes the bad news in manufacturing and med devices is behind it and will not recur, but declined to give details.

qa_highlights.question: Sudheer Guntupalli asked whether soft Q4 net new TCV reflects slippage, and whether 15%-plus steady-state margin is conservative given recent beats.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said clients are delaying decisions and deals are pushed to Q1, not lost. CFO said steady-state margin stays at 15%-plus, with erosion from sales, leadership and AI-orchestration investments, ramp-up effects and front-ended productivity commitments.

qa_highlights.question: Dipesh Mehta (Emkay) asked for the revenue impact of exiting low-margin business and the deal intake needed to resume QoQ growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 200 bps of FY26 growth went away from exiting low-margin and non-strategic deals, including the working-day effect. It gave no quarterly deal-intake target, only that order booking will be substantially better than FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Sandeep Shah (Equirus) asked why the new restructuring and leadership changes will work this time, and whether benefits will show in FY28 rather than FY27.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is disappointed, that earlier hires did not deliver and some were changed, and that sellers will rise about 40% by end of Q2 FY27. It said pipeline is already improving QoQ and that order booking and then revenue must follow.

qa_highlights.question: Priyank Chheda (Vallum) asked about the dividend payout versus cash build-up and the lack of pipeline or guidance disclosure.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the dividend is linked to PAT, which was similar year on year, and the Board will decide on surplus cash and inform shareholders when a call is taken. Management said small-company volatility is why it does not guide and that it will focus on sales and order book.

qa_highlights.question: Pulkit Chawla (360 ONE) asked what prevents guiding to Q1 growth and quantification of Q4 one-offs.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said market volatility is the reason it will not commit. CFO quantified Q4 benefits at about 340 bps in total: about 170 bps from forex and about 170 bps from lower performance-linked and leave-encashment provisions, and lower employee equity cost after three exits. The non-forex items will not recur.

capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or utilisation figures were disclosed on the call.

Sales capacity: management plans to grow the sales team 30-40% YoY by mid-FY27, with about 40% more sellers by end of Q2 FY27; hiring is weighted to the US, with a large portion of new sellers in US manufacturing.
Investment areas cited: AI orchestration layer, AI platforms (Cogito), leadership across service lines, partnerships and domain/service-line capabilities; no quantified spend was given.
Sales and support headcount was slightly down QoQ in Q4 while sales and marketing headcount rose, per the analyst's reading, which management confirmed as G&A reduction.
Lower ETR from FY27 as the incremental US federal tax provision is limited to FY26; ETR expected to settle closer to historical levels.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 revenue $145.3 mn, down 3.7% QoQ in constant currency and in dollar terms; INR revenue flat at +0.1% QoQ to INR 1,348.6 crore. FY26 revenue down 6% in USD and 1.2% in INR, with management citing 6.5% constant-currency degrowth in the Q&A.
Q4 TCV $208 mn, +3% QoQ and second straight quarter above $200 mn; Q4 net new TCV described as very soft, with clients delaying decisions. Around 38% of FY26 order booking came from existing clients.
About 200 bps of FY26 growth removed by exiting low-margin and non-strategic deals (includes effect of fewer working days in Q4).

AI deals require upfront productivity commitments and savings underwriting, causing revenue deflation in the immediate and medium term; outcome-based deals are operational-outcome linked and mostly fixed-price.

Verticals: E&U grew 1.8% QoQ (only vertical to grow); Life Sciences (MedTech) was the largest degrowth due to a client-specific operational issue; Manufacturing and BFSI degrew (BFSI on furloughs in Q3 and fewer working days in Q4; mainly T&M).
Competition: larger players are bidding for mid-sized deals as AI makes the playing field more level; management sees this as an opportunity for smaller firms too.
Management says client spending in BFSI remains stable but is shifting from traditional services to AI-related work (P&C insurance, payments, asset management); no increase in the addressable pool.

growth.why: No revenue guidance given; management cites volatility and says demand is very soft, with growth hoped for in H2 order booking and backed only by sales hiring (30-40% sales team growth by mid-FY27) and no quantified capacity, orders or contracts, so backing is vague.
